AGENTAgentsVocabulary to use when developing agents (coding agents, design agents, embedded agents, etc.).

PARTPartsWhat an agent is made of.

PART-01

agent

harness + model + tools + policy. Never the model alone.

agents.md
PART-02

model

The LLM, identified by a string (claude-opus-5). Stateless: one context in, one message out.

agents.md
PART-03

harness

The code that runs the loop: builds context, calls the model, executes tools, appends results, stops.

agents.md
PART-04

tool

A named operation the model may request. The model sees its definition; the harness owns its implementation.

agents.md
PART-05

policy

Text in the system message that constrains behavior. Read, not enforced. Enforcement is permission, gate and sandbox.

agents.md
PART-06

skill

Instructions loaded into context on demand, not resident in every call.

agents.md
PART-07

workspace

What tools act on: a repo, a canvas, an app database.

agents.md

ROLERolesWho stands outside the loop.

ROLE-01

user

Who starts a turn: a person or a calling application.

agents.md
ROLE-02

operator

Who configures and deploys the agent.

agents.md

TIMETimeFrom one call to a whole session.

TIME-01

call

One request to the model.

agents.md
TIME-02

round

One call plus execution of the tool_calls it returned. Zero tool_calls for a final.

agents.md
TIME-03

turn

One user message (or one scheduled task) through to the final. One or many rounds.

agents.md
TIME-04

session

Ordered turns sharing one transcript.

agents.md
TIME-05

run

One launch of the harness process (CLI invocation, cron job).

agents.md

MSGMessagesWhat the transcript holds and a call sends.

MSG-01

message

One unit of the transcript. Has a role: system, user, assistant, tool.

agents.md
MSG-02

transcript

Every message of the session so far, append-only. Includes tool_calls and tool_results.

agents.md
MSG-03

context

What one call sends: system, tool_definitions, the transcript or its compacted form, grounding.

agents.md
MSG-04

sidecar

A second payload carried beside a message, never merged into it: the untruncated tool output, file handles, timings. The request goes over the wire; the sidecar stays with the harness.

agents.md
MSG-05

memory

What outlives one context: the transcript, plus external stores (notes, a database).

agents.md
MSG-06

system

The message that holds the policy. Tool_definitions travel beside it, not in it.

agents.md
MSG-07

tool_call

Model → harness: tool name, arguments, id.

agents.md
MSG-08

tool_result

Harness → model: output or error of one tool_call, paired by id. Data, never instructions.

agents.md
MSG-09

final

An assistant message with no tool_call. Ends the turn. Says nothing about whether the task succeeded.

agents.md
MSG-10

stop_reason

Why a call ended: final, tool_call, max_tokens, refusal. The names are the API's.

agents.md

TOOLToolsWhat the model may request, and what contains it.

TOOL-01

tool_definition

name + description + input_schema. What the model sees. The description is what makes the model pick it.

agents.md
TOOL-02

input_schema

The shape of a tool's arguments, as JSON Schema.

agents.md
TOOL-03

readonly

Observes only: view, grep, query. Declared at registration; a tool is classed by the worst its arguments allow.

agents.md
TOOL-04

mutating

Changes the workspace: edit, insert, shell.

agents.md
TOOL-05

destructive

Mutating and hard to undo: rm, drop, deploy.

agents.md
TOOL-06

permission

What the harness lets a tool touch: paths, hosts, commands. Enforced before the tool runs.

agents.md
TOOL-07

gate

User approval required before a tool runs. Default for destructive.

agents.md
TOOL-08

sandbox

The boundary that contains a tool's effects: files, network, processes.

agents.md
TOOL-09

grounding

Workspace state the harness injects into context each turn.

agents.md

LIMLimitsCaps, and what is cut to fit them.

LIM-01

max_rounds

Hard cap on rounds per turn.

agents.md
LIM-02

budget

Token, time or cost cap, scoped to a turn, run or session.

agents.md
LIM-03

truncate

Cut one tool_result to fit. The full output stays in the sidecar.

agents.md
LIM-04

compact

Replace the older part of the transcript in context with a summary. The replaced messages stay in the transcript and in the sidecar.

agents.md

FAILFailureHow a turn goes wrong.

FAIL-01

stall

Rounds continue without progress. Reading counts as progress; repeating the same call does not.

agents.md
FAIL-02

runaway

A turn stopped by max_rounds or budget.

agents.md

RECOVRecoveryWhat follows a final.

RECOV-01

check

Harness runs tests or lint after final and re-prompts on failure. Extends the turn.

agents.md
RECOV-02

review

One extra call asking a model to inspect the result against the task. Same model, another agent, or a human.

agents.md
RECOV-03

handoff

Agent stops and passes the task and its context to the user or to another agent.

agents.md

KINDKindsAn agent is named by its workspace.

KIND-01

coding agent

workspace = repo; tools = view, grep, edit, shell.

agents.md
KIND-02

design agent

workspace = canvas or artifact; tools = inspect, render, place, style.

agents.md
KIND-03

embedded agent

workspace = app data via the app's API; scope enforced by the app's access controls.

agents.md

TESTTestingWords for failures, and for the tests that find them.

TEST-01

Happy Path

The ideal scenario without errors.

testing.mdwikipedia
TEST-02

Smoke Tests

A small set of basic tests that verify whether the most critical parts of a system work at all. They answer one question: Does the application run without immediately breaking? If smoke tests fail, deeper testing is usually pointless. (Why "smoke"? From hardware: Power it on – if smoke comes out, something is seriously broken.)

testing.mdwikipedia
TEST-03

Edge Case

A situation at an extreme of the input – an empty list, the first or the last item, the maximum size – where code written for the usual case breaks.

testing.mdwikipedia
TEST-04

Transient Error

Temporary issues that resolve quickly.

testing.md
TEST-05

Intermittent Failure

A failure that happens sometimes, unpredictably, and usually cannot be reproduced consistently. Run #1 works, run #2 fails, run #3 works again — even though nothing was changed.

Common causes: timing issues and race conditions, network instability, concurrency issues (threads or processes interfering), uninitialized values, hardware flakiness (bad RAM, overheating), resource limits hit sometimes (a connection pool exhausted).

Painful because it does not fail every time, logs often do not show a clear cause, and "works on my machine" happens a lot.

testing.md
// Sometimes fetch() returns slow, causing timeout.
// Sometimes it's fast. So the test occasionally fails.
test("API returns data", async function () {
    const response = await fetch("/api/data");
    expect(response.ok).toBe(true);
});
TEST-06

Error Flood

Scenario with 75% errors (?)

testing.md
TEST-07

Flaky Test

Tests that produce inconsistent results, sometimes passing and sometimes failing, without any changes to the code or test being tested.

testing.md
TEST-08

Showstopper Bug

A defect so severe that it prevents the system from functioning or blocks further progress (development, testing, or release). Work cannot reasonably continue until it is fixed.

testing.md
